title: Creating Bacterial Glycerol Stocks for Long-term Storage
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf5qjq5w

steps.title: Inoculate liquid culture
steps.instruction: Grow bacteria in liquid medium according to the referenced protocol until an overnight culture is obtained.

steps.title: Prepare 50% glycerol
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 % glycerol with deionized water to a final concentration of 50 % (v/v) to make the glycerol solution.

steps.title: Use appropriate tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the 50 % glycerol solution into screw‑top tubes or cryotubes; avoid snap‑top tubes because they can open unexpectedly at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label glycerol stock tubes
steps.instruction: Write the sample information on both the tube and its lid with a permanent marker before freezing.

steps.title: Combine culture with glycerol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of the overnight bacterial culture to 500 µL of the 50 % glycerol in a 2 mL screw‑top tube or cryotube and gently mix.

steps.title: Shake glycerol mixture
steps.instruction: Invert or vortex the tube 5–6 times until a uniform, single‑phase solution is observed; ensure no layers are present.

steps.title: Freeze glycerol stock
steps.instruction: Place the sealed tube at –80 °C. The stock remains stable for years if kept continuously frozen; minimize freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Handle stock on dry ice
steps.instruction: When moving or streaking, keep the tube on dry ice to prevent thawing and improve shelf life.

steps.title: Recover bacteria from stock
steps.instruction: Open the frozen tube and, without allowing it to thaw, use a sterile loop, toothpick, or pipette tip to scrape a small amount of frozen bacteria from the top, then follow the Streaking and Isolating Bacteria on a LB Agar Plate protocol.
